correctness.rationale: Permutation averaging shows some optimal center is diagonal. At \(c\mathbf1\), containment is equivalent to radius no larger than \(c\) and every support distance \((R_k-kc)/\sqrt{k}\). Their crossings with the coordinate-facet distance are the values \(a_k\). Writing \(k=t^2\), the derivative numerator of the continuous extension is strictly decreasing, so no interior minimum exists and only \(k=1,m\) can be active. Comparing those endpoints gives the formula and transition. The active upper constraint together with all coordinate lower constraints forces every coordinate of any optimal center to equal the radius, proving uniqueness. Representative independent checks reproduced both regimes and \(\mathcal P(2,1)\)'s right-triangle inradius.

value.rationale: Partial permutohedra are an established natural polytope family, and Euclidean inradius plus Chebyshev center is a standard geometric invariant not supplied by their known combinatorial descriptions. The exact formula also reveals a sharp, parameter-dependent change in the active facet family, giving structural information beyond a single numerical radius.

final_claim: For \(m\ge2\) and \(n\ge m-1\), the Euclidean inradius of the partial permutohedron is \(\min\{n/2,\sqrt m(2n-m+1)/(2(\sqrt m+1))\}\); the inscribed-ball center is uniquely \(r\mathbf1\), with the stated singleton-versus-total-sum tangency transition at \(n=m+\sqrt m\).
limitations: Restricted to \(n\ge m-1\) and Euclidean balls.
